selection: First two episodes in each sorted LongMemEval v1 question-type group (12); first 12 SHA256-ranked LoCoMo v1 episodes (12). Corpus text supplies background only; this is not benchmark QA accuracy.
target: Unique deterministic 24-hex synthetic code plus balanced randomly assigned ALPHA/BETA route preference; all evidence generated after training.
summary: One actual model-generated summary per episode, retained unchanged across paired arms; no filtering by success.
primary: Paired difference in target-route selection rate versus never-seen, averaged across two option orders within episode.
secondary: exact code emission on either direct probe
reachable CPython memoization-cache key recovery before and after explicit clear
analysis: All 24 episodes, no exclusion; 10000 episode-cluster paired bootstrap samples with fixed seed; no pooling option-order trials as independent episodes.

hypotheses.H5: Source-only deletion and one-time purge followed by snapshot replay permit more behavioral influence than never-seen.
hypotheses.H6: The full overlay with fresh caller context yields the same supplied evidence as never-seen after snapshot replay; resulting equality is a construction check, not proof of model unlearning.
hypotheses.H7: An unmanaged model-written live summary can retain influence despite clean managed storage.
hypotheses.H8: The v1 memoizer retains reachable plaintext keys after deletion; explicitly clearing it removes those keys from this reachable cache.

boundaries: One small quantized model, temperature zero
Oracle scope labels and serialized storage operations
No neural embedding inversion or KV-tensor forensics
No physical heap erasure, provider log deletion, or model weight unlearning
Research response logs intentionally retain synthetic targets
Prompt caching disabled but no physical cache erasure claimed
